saw_lines: Buyers of everyday clothing pick a piece by fit and fabric, then come back only when the first one wears out.
So the sale is won in the first line, where a buyer decides if fit and fabric are worth a click.
Your site quotes 200 years of trench coats and jeans, yet 0 of 29 ads use a number. Put that line on the creative and open two ads with a quote.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 28 Oct 2026
points: Your site quotes 200 years of trench coats and jeans, yet 0 of 29 ads use a proof number, so new buyers have nothing to check. Put that line on the creative and open two ads with a customer quote.
Your site offers 10% off your first order yet 0 of 21 ads mention it, so a new buyer has no reason to act. Put the 10% first order offer in the opening line of three new ads and on the creative.

13 of 21 copy ads open on the same winter line, so most of your copy sounds identical to a buyer. Build two new angles from your denim and knitwear, like fit and the Marylebone store, and run them against it.

Your site promises free worldwide shipping, yet 0 of 29 ads mention shipping or delivery, so buyers must click away to learn it. Open the first sentence of three new ads with the free worldwide shipping line, before the collection name.
